_comment: SOURCE OF TRUTH for the AI Website Creator roadmap rendered at /ai-dev-kit/ai-website-creator. The AI Website Creator is NOT an extension — it lives in the AI Dev Kit (skills + docs/recipes + the generalized vertical-template library) and drives the plugin's existing fresh-build and Site Converter paths. Task `status` is maintained by `npm run roadmap:site-creator` (scripts/gen-roadmap.mjs), which resolves the source tree via `cloneDir` (the AI Dev Kit push clone) and flips a task to `done` when everything in its `detect` block exists there. Nothing is built yet, so every unpinned task is `planned` — correct before any code exists. Hand-edit title/detail/detect freely; set `pin: true` on a concept task with no single file footprint.

milestones.title: Phase 1 · The archetype catalogue
milestones.goal: A curated set of **section archetypes**, each a small recipe that emits **page-builder JSON + Unyson+ shortcodes + Animation Engine effects**, with colour and type coming from **Theme Settings presets** rather than baked onto each element. Start where the demand is — heroes, navbars, feature grids, CTAs, footers, marquees — not at a hundred thin entries.

tasks.title: Recipe format
tasks.detail: One document shape every recipe follows: *when to use it*, *the composition* (the exact shortcode arrangement as a builder-JSON template), *the motion* (which Animation Engine effect pairs with it, and the restrained default), *the tokens* (which Theme Settings presets it expects), and *a live preview* (a link to our own demo page). The format is the contract the composition guide and the create-site skill both read.

tasks.title: Hero recipes
tasks.detail: The highest-frequency archetype by a wide margin. A handful of genuinely good heroes (centered, split, editorial-oversized, media-backed), each as a builder-JSON template with restrained motion and preset-driven type.

tasks.title: Navbar recipes
tasks.detail: Universal header patterns built on the Header/Footer Builder: logo, primary nav from the sitemap, an accessible mobile menu, an active-page state, and the primary CTA.

tasks.title: Feature-grid recipes
tasks.detail: Icon-box and card grids for features, services and benefits, mapped to the real shortcodes with preset-owned card skins (never per-element copies).

tasks.title: CTA recipes
tasks.detail: Conversion blocks — banner CTAs, split CTAs, inverted full-bleed CTAs — with the button skin living on its colour preset.

tasks.title: Footer recipes
tasks.detail: Universal footer patterns on the Footer Builder: brand summary, navigation, the primary conversion path, and legal links once they exist.

tasks.title: Marquee & logo-strip recipes
tasks.detail: Moving strips for logos, words and proof, using the native marquee element with reduced-motion handling built in.

milestones.title: Phase 2 · The style library
milestones.goal: A curated set of named **design directions** a person can pick from — the "make the design <style>" input. A style is not a theme file; it is a mapping from a look to **Theme Settings presets** (palette, fonts, radius, borders, spacing), the **Animation Engine** register that fits it (instant vs. cinematic), and the section treatments that express its personality. We take the *taxonomy and the design thinking* from the public design-prompt libraries; every style is re-authored here in our own vocabulary, because those prompts describe React and Tailwind components, not page-builder output.

tasks.title: Style model
tasks.detail: How a named style resolves to a design system: the Theme Settings preset set it writes, the type pairing, the radius/border/texture rules, and the Animation Engine defaults. One model so every style is described the same way and the picker can list them.

tasks.title: Map to the existing aesthetic skills
tasks.detail: Several directions already exist as design skills — a refined default, minimalist, brutalist, and a high-end "expensive-agency" look. A style entry points at the matching skill where one exists, and only carries a new recipe where there is a genuine gap, so the library reuses rather than duplicates.

tasks.title: Seed the high-value styles
tasks.detail: A first set drawn from the demand we can see: a monochrome editorial look (pure black and white, serif hero, zero radius, line textures, inversion hover), a newsprint look, a Swiss/Bauhaus grid look, a modern dark look, a terminal look, a luxury look, and a kinetic/motion-led look. Each is a design direction expressed as Theme Settings presets plus section treatments — authored here, never copied.

tasks.title: The style picker
tasks.detail: The intake step that offers the styles as an enumerated choice (the "dropdown"), with a *describe-your-own* escape hatch so the curated set is never a cage. In the kit this is a choice in the create-site flow; in a later in-admin or hosted surface it becomes a visual picker with thumbnails — same list, no rework. **Waits on Phase 4.** The picker is a step in the create-site flow, and that flow does not exist yet — the seven styles are the list it will offer, so the library is ready for it. Building a picker before there is anything to pick into would be a UI with no behind it.

milestones.title: Phase 3 · The composition guide
milestones.goal: A catalogue of parts is not a site. This is the sequencing layer that turns a chosen style and a set of archetypes into a coherent page, and it slots onto the existing build protocol rather than replacing it: **design system first → chrome (header/footer) → sections, region by region → motion → ship gate.** The generator is no more allowed to skip to "write sections" than a careful human build is.

tasks.title: Composition guide
tasks.detail: The ordering rules, the page-shape heuristics (which archetypes a given page type wants, and in what sequence), and the hand-off into the build protocol's phases and gates.

tasks.title: Ship-gate wiring
tasks.detail: Every composed page carries the same accessibility, SEO and performance obligations as everything else we ship — reduced-motion handling, a sane Web Vitals cost, real content in the HTML — checked with the kit's `tools/measure` harness. A page that fails the gate does not ship.

milestones.title: Phase 4 · The create-site skill
milestones.goal: The single entry point the person runs in their own Claude Code / Cursor through the AI Dev Kit. One flow, four ways in: a plain-language **brief**, a **reference URL**, a **design reference** (screenshot / image), or a **vertical template**. It gathers a structured spec, then drives the build protocol (or the Site Converter for the URL and design-reference paths) to a finished, editable Unyson+ site.

tasks.title: Skill scaffold
tasks.detail: A `create-site` skill under the kit's reserved `skills/` folder: a `SKILL.md` that wires the intake, the style picker, the archetype catalogue, the composition guide and the ship gate into one routed flow.

tasks.title: Site spec
tasks.detail: A structured description of the site — business, pages, brand, style, sections, SEO, compliance — generalized from the CRM website generator's `site-spec.json`. The spec, not a prose prompt, is the source of truth the build reads.

tasks.title: Input: a brief
tasks.detail: From a plain-language brief ("a barber shop, warm and dark, booking-led") to the spec: propose a sitemap, pick a style and archetypes, fill copy, choose a palette. The fresh-build path — the only input that skips capture.

tasks.title: Input: a reference URL
tasks.detail: Hand the URL to the capture service and Site Converter, which produce a native build; the creator then refines it through the same composition and ship-gate steps. Reuses the converter end to end rather than re-implementing it.

tasks.title: Input: a design reference
tasks.detail: From an uploaded screenshot or image: read the look (palette, type, spacing, treatment) into a style and tokens, without copying the reference's content, logos or distinctive layout. Captures the design, builds original content on it.

tasks.title: Input: a vertical template
tasks.detail: Pick an industry starting point and let the creator customize it — the CRM-generator pattern, generalized (see Phase 6).

tasks.title: Build rules ported from the field
tasks.detail: The durable rules a good WordPress build follows, as the creator's own: editable builder output (never static HTML or one big Custom HTML block), one universal header and footer, drafts not published until asked, native Unyson+ / theme SEO configured against the real business details, and no invented testimonials, metrics, pricing or claims.

milestones.title: Phase 5 · Content maintenance
milestones.goal: After the site exists, keep it growing. A separate flow for creating a page or post around a topic: research and recommend, wait for approval, draft and optimize for SEO, then publish only on an explicit second approval. Two gates, never one.

tasks.title: Content skill
tasks.detail: A `content` flow in the kit that uses the existing site and its records as the source of truth, so it never re-asks for business, audience or brand facts already known.

tasks.title: Research & recommend (gate 1)
tasks.detail: Study the sitemap, internal links, the topic and search intent; return page-vs-post, angles, titles, a heading structure, the internal links to add, and the specific expert questions only the owner can answer. Wait for approval before drafting.

tasks.title: Draft & optimize
tasks.detail: Create an editable draft in the current design system, set title, permalink, meta and schema, run the native SEO checks, add genuinely-relevant internal links, and never keyword-stuff or invent facts to satisfy a score.

tasks.title: Publish (gate 2)
tasks.detail: Publish the approved draft only on an explicit go-ahead — do not rewrite it — then verify the public URL, canonical and SEO metadata.

milestones.title: Phase 6 · Vertical templates
milestones.goal: Generalize the CRM website generator into the creator's vertical-template layer, so an industry is a starting point rather than a separate product. The CRM Generator becomes the first vertical; its industry presets become the model for the shared library.

tasks.title: Vertical-template format
tasks.detail: The generalized, non-industry form of the CRM generator's industry presets: pages, copy, forms, the spec and the build wording for a vertical, as data the create-site flow reads.

tasks.title: CRM as the first vertical
tasks.detail: Fold the CRM website generator in as the first vertical-template provider: its spec and prompts already drive the AI Dev Kit fresh-build path, so it is the proof the pattern works. The CRM pipeline, forms and newsletter CRM come switched on for this vertical.

tasks.title: Further verticals
tasks.detail: A handful more, drawn from the generator's existing set (local business, professional service, ecommerce, SaaS), each a vertical template the creator can start from and customize.

milestones.title: Phase 7 · The style gallery
milestones.goal: A rendered Unyson+ example per style, so a person can see before they pick — and so the gallery doubles as proof of what the creator makes. Built on our own demos network, listed on the demos home, never a copy of anyone else's preview media.

tasks.title: A demo page per style
tasks.detail: One native Unyson+ page per seeded style, each the same content rendered through that style's presets, so the differences are the design and nothing else.

tasks.title: Listed on the demos home
tasks.detail: Each style demo gets a card on the demos home grid, so it is discoverable and never orphaned, per the house rule for demos.

milestones.title: Phase 8 · Product surface
milestones.goal: Make it easy for a non-expert to drive. v1 is the kit itself — install the AI Dev Kit, point your agent at your WordPress, run the create-site flow — with onboarding that explains exactly that. An in-admin wizard and a hosted web app are later surfaces on the same proven engine, not v1.

tasks.title: Onboarding
tasks.detail: The guided "how to use it" path: install the kit, connect the agent to the target WordPress, and run the create-site flow — written so someone who has never used Claude Code can follow it.

tasks.title: In-admin wizard (future)
tasks.detail: The AI Assistant extension drives the whole flow inside wp-admin, so no CLI is needed. A later surface on the same engine.

tasks.title: Hosted app (future)
tasks.detail: A hosted web app that builds and deploys into the person's WordPress. The biggest surface and the most infrastructure; only once the engine is proven.
